audits.title: Optimising stroke prevention in patients with atrial fibrillation: application of the GRASP-AF audit tool in a UK general practice cohort.
audits.standard: Oral anticoagulation for AF patients at high stroke risk (CHA2DS2-VASc ≥2 or CHADS2 ≥1), using the GRASP-AF tool

cycle1.result: Of those with CHA2DS2-VASc ≥2, 39.7% were not receiving appropriate OAC; of those with CHADS2 ≥1, 39.5% were not.

audits.other_findings: Antiplatelet monotherapy used in 33-40% of high-risk patients; OAC reduced stroke (OR 0.60) and death (OR 0.54) over 12 months.
audits.citation: Shantsila E, Wolff A, Lip GY, Lane DA. Optimising stroke prevention in patients with atrial fibrillation: application of the GRASP-AF audit tool in a UK general practice cohort. Br J Gen Pract. 2015;65(630):e16-23. doi:10.3399/bjgp15x683113. PMID: 25548312.

audits.title: Risk stratification and stroke prevention therapy care gaps in Canadian atrial fibrillation patients (from the Co-ordinated National Network to Engage Physicians in the Care and Treatment of Patients With Atrial Fibrillation chart audit).
audits.standard: Formal stroke (CHADS2) and bleeding (HAS-BLED) risk assessment; suggested warfarin time in therapeutic range target of ≥70%

cycle1.result: No annual stroke risk assessment in 15% and no formal tool in 33%; bleeding risk not assessed in 25% and no formal tool in 47%. Warfarin TTR ≥70% in 1,827 (55%), 50-69% in 674 (20%) and <50% in 845 (25%); median TTR 73%.

audits.other_findings: Physicians overestimated bleeding risk in 26%; therapy was warfarin 58%, dabigatran 22%, rivaroxaban 14%, apixaban <1%.
audits.citation: Patel AD, Tan MK, Angaran P, Bell AD, Berall M, Bucci C, et al.. Risk stratification and stroke prevention therapy care gaps in Canadian atrial fibrillation patients (from the Co-ordinated National Network to Engage Physicians in the Care and Treatment of Patients With Atrial Fibrillation chart audit). Am J Cardiol. 2015;115(5):641-646. doi:10.1016/j.amjcard.2014.12.022. PMID: 25727083.

audits.title: Contemporary utilization of antithrombotic therapy for stroke prevention in patients with atrial fibrillation: an audit in an Australian hospital setting.
audits.standard: Anticoagulation of eligible patients (CHA2DS2-VASc score of 2 or more, no bleeding risk factors)
audits.setting: Australian hospital, inpatients with atrial fibrillation

cycle1.result: 84.0% discharged on antithrombotics; anticoagulants (± antiplatelets) 52.0% (two-thirds warfarin, the rest NOACs), antiplatelets 33.0%. Among 'most eligible' patients, 46.0% were not anticoagulated on discharge.

audits.other_findings: Patients aged 75 and over were less likely to receive NOACs (14.0% vs 28.0%, p = 0.01); patients with renal impairment were more likely to receive warfarin than NOACs (OR 3.6).
audits.citation: Pandya EY, Anderson E, Chow C, Wang Y, Bajorek B. Contemporary utilization of antithrombotic therapy for stroke prevention in patients with atrial fibrillation: an audit in an Australian hospital setting. Ther Adv Drug Saf. 2018;9(2):97-111. doi:10.1177/2042098617744926. PMID: 29387335.

audits.title: Anticoagulation management services in community pharmacy: Feasibility of implementing a quality improvement programme through a practice-based research network.
audits.standard: Quality indicators for anticoagulation management services
audits.setting: 37 community pharmacies in a practice-based research network, Quebec

cycle1.result: Mean global QI score 39.1% for VKAs and 12.3% for DOACs.

audits.intervention: Audit and feedback on quality indicators plus a personalised training programme with online videos

cycle2.result: QI scores rose by 12.5 percentage points for VKAs and 9.9 points for DOACs.

audits.other_findings: Pharmacist knowledge score rose from 68.7% by 4.3 points.
audits.citation: Chartrand M, Lalonde L, Cantin A, Lahaie A, Odobasic B, Tremblay MP, et al.. Anticoagulation management services in community pharmacy: Feasibility of implementing a quality improvement programme through a practice-based research network. J Clin Pharm Ther. 2018;43(6):877-887. doi:10.1111/jcpt.12745. PMID: 30019341.

audits.title: Oral anticoagulant treatment in rheumatoid arthritis patients with atrial fibrillation results of an international audit.
audits.standard: Guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation for AF with CHA2DS2-VASc of 2 or more in males and 3 or more in females

cycle1.result: 288 (3.8%) had AF; of 255 (88.5%) with a CHA2DS2-VASc score indicating anticoagulation, 164 (64.3%) were anticoagulated.

audits.other_findings: AF was associated with older age, male sex, atherosclerotic disease, heart failure and hypertension.
audits.citation: Semb AG, Rollefstad S, Sexton J, Ikdahl E, Crowson CS, van Riel P, et al.. Oral anticoagulant treatment in rheumatoid arthritis patients with atrial fibrillation results of an international audit. Int J Cardiol Heart Vasc. 2022;42:101117. doi:10.1016/j.ijcha.2022.101117. PMID: 36118256.
